name: Urartians
desc: A mountain kingdom of fortresses on rocky ridges, great canals and vast wine cellars, whose god Haldi was carried into battle and whose name lives on in Mount Ararat.
source: Urartian royal inscriptions in cuneiform; excavations at Van, Karmir Blur (Teishebaini) and Erebuni

cautious: sealed a hundred great jars of wine in the cellar before the snow
belligerent: held the pass against raiders through a winter night
devout: carried the bronze shield of Haldi in the spring procession

inventions.name: Menua's Canal
inventions.source: King Menua's canal (c. 800 BCE) carries water some 70 km to Van, and still runs today; locals call it the Shamiram canal
inventions.desc: A stone-lined channel cut along the mountainside to the fields: farm plots yield 25% more.
inventions.hint: Needs farming and Polished Stone Tools, and builders who quarry.

inventions.name: Ridge Fortress
inventions.source: Urartian fortresses such as Van and Ayanis sit on rock ridges, with walls of huge cut stones
inventions.desc: Walls of fitted stone along a rock spine: +2 defence.

inventions.name: Griffin Cauldron
inventions.source: Bronze cauldrons with bull and griffin heads round the rim were made in Urartu and copied as far as Greece and Etruria
inventions.desc: A great bronze bowl ringed with bulls' and griffins' heads, for the god's feasts: rites bring 10% more devotion, +2 mood.

inventions.name: Cellar of Great Jars
inventions.source: The storerooms of Teishebaini (Karmir Blur) held hundreds of huge jars, each marked with its capacity
inventions.desc: Rows of jars taller than a man, half buried in the cool earth: the stores hold 30 more food, food spoils 8% slower.

foods.name: Highland Wine
foods.source: Areni-1 cave nearby holds the oldest known winery (c. 4100 BCE); Urartian kings boasted of the vineyards they planted
foods.desc: Grapes trodden in a stone vat and left to work in great jars: +3 mood.

foods.name: Dried Tarekh
foods.desc: Little fish from the soda lake, salted and dried by the thousand: food spoils 10% slower, hunger grows 5% slower.

finds.name: Tarekh Shoals
finds.source: The pearl mullet of Lake Van, the only fish that lives in its soda water, swims up the rivers each spring to spawn
finds.desc: Silver fish crowding up the stream in spring, easy to scoop by the basketful.

finds.name: Apricot Trees
finds.desc: Golden fruit of the highland orchards; the Romans called it the Armenian plum.

people.name: Ulushu
people.desc: He reads the slope of a mountain like a page.
memory: led the spring water around the hill to the barley terraces

people.name: Melardi
people.desc: A hunter of the high passes, never cold, never lost.
memory: brought down a mountain goat on the cliffs above the lake

people.name: Tariria
people.source: An inscription near Van names 'the vineyard of Tariria, daughter of Menua'
people.desc: A princess who owned a vineyard of her own, one of very few Urartian women named in stone.

people.name: Menua
people.source: Inscriptions along the canal: 'Whoever destroys this inscription, may Haldi destroy him'
people.desc: The king who cut the canal to Van and wrote his name along it every few miles.

people.name: Dadu
people.text: a travelling smith with a sack of moulds, who casts bulls' heads and griffins for any chief who will feed him.
memory: cast a cauldron so big it took six men to lift
people.desc: A smith of the kind whose cauldrons travelled from Urartu to Greece.

people.name: Argishti
people.label: Argishti, Founder of Erebuni
people.desc: He founds the city that will become Yerevan. Crafting 7, Combat 5.

people.name: Sarduri
people.label: Sarduri, King of Kings
people.desc: A warrior king of the mountains. Combat 8.

people.name: Ara
people.label: Ara the Beautiful
people.desc: So fair a queen went to war for him. Foraging 5, Lore 5, beloved by all.

events.title: The Enemy Marches on the Temple
events.source: In 714 BCE Sargon II of Assyria sacked Musasir, the holy city of Haldi, and listed every treasure he carried off
events.text: Word comes that a great army is crossing the mountains toward our shrine, where the god's shields and cauldrons are kept.

options.label: Hide the treasures in the caves
options.result: The god's treasures vanish into the mountain. When the army arrives, it finds bare walls.

options.label: Stand and fight at the shrine
options.result: The warriors gather at the shrine. Scouts are already in the trees.

events.title: The Fish Come Up the River
events.text: The streams are so full of silver fish that children catch them with their hands. Everyone goes down to the water with baskets.

events.title: The Snow Closes the Passes
events.text: Snow has closed every pass. For months nothing will come up from the valleys. The elders ask how to face the long winter.

options.label: Live in the cellars
options.result: Families move down among the great jars, where the earth keeps the frost out.

options.label: Feast through the dark
options.result: Wine is drawn from the great jars and the winter is sung away.

tales.name: Ara and the Queen of Assyria
tales.source: Movses Khorenatsi, History of Armenia (5th–8th century CE)
tales.text: The queen of Assyria heard of a king in the mountains so beautiful that she sent for him to be her husband. Ara refused, for he loved his own wife. So she made war to take him alive, but he fell in the battle, and she grieved for him and asked the winged spirits to lick his wounds and wake him.

tales.name: The Gate of Haldi
tales.source: Meher Kapısı near Van, a rock-cut niche with an inscription of Ishpuini and Menua listing offerings to the gods
tales.text: On the cliff a false door is cut into the rock. It does not open for people. On the great days the god Haldi steps out of it, and so the oxen and sheep are brought before it, so many for Haldi, so many for the Storm God, so many for the Sun.
tales.moral: the gods have their own doors

tales.name: The Mountain Where the Boat Rested
tales.source: Later Armenian and Christian tradition placed Noah's landing on the great mountain of Urartu, Masis (Ararat)
tales.text: When the great flood covered the world, the last boat drifted until it struck the twin peaks in the north, where the snow never melts. The people who came down from it planted the first vineyard on the slopes below. That is why our vines are the oldest.
tales.moral: after the flood, plant a vine

tales.name: The Vineyard of Tariria
tales.source: A story made up around Tariria's inscription
tales.text: The king gave his daughter a stony slope that no one wanted. She carried earth up in baskets, planted vines, and dug a little channel from her father's canal. When the vintage came, her wine was the best in the kingdom, and the king had her name carved on a stone so no one could take the slope away.
